objectives: Students will be able to apply research skills to educational problems.
Design, implementation, and evaluation of scholarly inquiry in educational leadership and administration conducted under the supervision of a faculty member.
Students will be able to apply concepts and theories learned in previous coursework to a real-world project, demonstrating their understanding through practical implementation.
Students will develop skills in defining project scope, creating timelines, allocating resources, managing risks, and effectively executing a project plan.
Students will practice research methodologies, collect and analyze relevant data, interpret results, and draw meaningful conclusions.
Students will be able to identify and analyze complex problems, develop creative solutions, and evaluate their effectiveness in a project context.
Students will be able to effectively communicate project findings and ideas both verbally and in writing to diverse audiences and peers.
Students will gain experience in professional practices relevant to their field, such as project documentation, presentation skills, and ethical considerations.
topics: Specific activities are selected by supervisor.
Design, implementation, and evaluation of scholarly inquiry in educational leadership and administration conducted under
Project Topic Selection and Proposal Development
Identifying stakeholders and project scope
Developing a detailed project proposal Design
Selecting appropriate methods (qualitative, mixed methods, creative applications)
Strategies for collection and/or development of resources
Ethical considerations Collection, Analysis, Creation
Procedures
Organization
Analysis or synthesis
Interpretation or reflection Project Implementation and Evaluation
Project development and implementation
Monitoring progress and making adjustments
